column5: You are standing in the middle of a financial district.
It is a busy weekday morning.
Right now, five and a half billion people are online.
Together, they send more than three hundred billion emails a day.
And ninety-five percent of the data between continents runs through cables on the bottom of the sea.
At first, it looks like a glitch.
Shops lock their doors, because they cannot take your money.
Nobody knows which way to turn.
Above the city, the planes grow fewer.
By evening, most of the windows are dark.
We just can't connect to it anymore.
